intro: The name "Sook Aroon" (happy dawn) sums this place up better than anything — Baan Sook Aroon Khao Kho is a small stay of about 6 rooms on a hillside in the Sadiao Phong area of Khao Kho District, Phetchabun Province, built around one moment of the day: the morning · the thing real reviews agree on most is that every room has a private balcony facing the sunrise and the sea of fog that drifts over the valley — wake up, open the balcony door and the view is right there, no driving out to fight for a spot at a viewpoint · it is a small pet-friendly stay with a shared kitchen, a BBQ corner and a garden, close to the Khao Kho Palace viewpoint · from about THB 1,000–1,800/night, with real review scores around 8.6 on Agoda/Trip.com and as high as about 9.3 on Booking.com

body.html: The big picture and who it suits — the shortest way to put it: Baan Sook Aroon Khao Kho is a small holiday-home-style stay on a hillside in the Sadiao Phong area of Khao Kho District, Phetchabun Province, and the one thing it sells clearly is "the morning" · it is not a luxury resort with hundreds of rooms and a big pool, not a heavily themed photo-all-day stay — it is a small place of about 6 rooms that leans on quiet, privacy, and the sunrise and sea of fog you can see from your own balcony · pulling together real reviews from Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com, Traveloka and several Khao Kho review pages, the picture is fairly consistent: the people this suits best are couples who want a quiet, romantic stay, small families, and anyone who wants to wake up to a sea of fog without getting up early to fight for a viewpoint rather than those hunting for a luxury resort with every amenity · another group who say it is worth it are pet lovers, because this is one of the Khao Kho stays that welcomes pets, so you can bring your dog or cat along · if you are expecting sleek modern rooms, a pool, a gym, or a varied buffet, set your expectations — this place sells simple, warm holiday-home comfort that the owners run themselves, more than the polish of a big hotel · put simply, if the goal of the trip is "wake up early, sip coffee and watch the fog drift by from the balcony," this place does that job squarely, at a price you can actually reach

Location and getting there — Baan Sook Aroon sits at about 127 Moo 2, Sadiao Phong Subdistrict, Khao Kho District, Phetchabun, on a hillside facing out over the valley · its biggest advantage is that it is close to the Khao Kho Palace viewpoint at only about 540 metres and View Ver Camp at about 980 metres, so you can reach the popular viewpoints in a few minutes — yet the stay itself is positioned where you can see the sea of fog from your own balcony without going anywhere · driving to Khao Kho's main sights from here is easy too — Khao Kho Palace, the Kanchanaphisek Pagoda, the Khao Kho wind-turbine field and the Khao Kho Memorial are all a short drive away · Wat Phra That Pha Sorn Kaew, Khao Kho's number-one highlight, is further out towards Khaem Son and takes roughly half an hour or more by car depending on where you stay · most people arrive from Bangkok by driving themselves via the Saraburi–Lom Sak route, about 5–6 hours, or by coach to Phetchabun town and then a vehicle up the mountain · the stay is about 38 kilometres from Phetchabun town and the nearest airport, with Phitsanulok being the more convenient main airport though it is further out · an important thing to know is that the road up to Khao Kho in the Sadiao Phong area is steep and winding, narrow in places — if you are driving yourself, check your vehicle and brakes carefully; in the rainy season the road is slippery and the fog rolls in thick with short visibility, so drive slowly and use your lights · with a small stay like this the parking spot may sometimes mean a short walk up a slope to the room, so if you have elderly travellers or a lot of luggage, ask the stay in advance

"The selling point is waking up early, opening the balcony door and the sea of fog is right there — no driving out to fight for a viewpoint · the stay is small and very quiet, the owner takes good care of you and is friendly, and you can bring your dog · at this price it is well worth it for the view you get."

Rooms and decor — Baan Sook Aroon is a small stay with roughly 5–6 rooms, and the room count varies slightly across platforms as listings are updated · what sets it apart from the usual small stay, and what gets talked about most, is that nearly every room has a private balcony facing the mountains and the sunrise — some are Queen or King rooms with a mountain-view balcony, and there is a family room for groups · the decor is simple, warm holiday-home style, leaning on natural tones that blend with the surrounding view, not the luxury or sleek minimalism of a boutique hotel · inside, the rooms have the essentials for a restful stay — a water heater, a TV, a fan or air conditioning depending on the room type, shelving, instant coffee, a mirror, a sofa and towels · most reviews agree that the rooms are very clean, the beds are comfortable, and above all the balcony view is well beyond the price · because this is a small, budget-friendly stay, the decor leans on simplicity and cleanliness rather than luxury · one thing to keep in mind: as a small stay on a hillside, some rooms may be compact, and soundproofing between rooms may not match a large building, so if quiet privacy matters to you, set your expectations · another thing to check before booking is the type of air conditioning and whether there are thick blankets, because the Sadiao Phong area of Khao Kho gets very cold in winter, especially at night and early morning, so a water heater and warm bedding make the stay much more comfortable · for families there are rooms that hold several people, good for a small group or for parents and kids

Facilities, pool and pets — being a small stay, the facilities at Baan Sook Aroon lean on simplicity but cover what you need for resting and cooking for yourself · there is a shared kitchen for guests to use together, a BBQ corner and a garden with a lounge area to step out into the cool air and do group activities · there is a small convenience store on site for essentials, a tent/camping area according to some platforms, and a front desk staffed 24 hours · for basic services there is free Wi-Fi in all rooms, free private parking, laundry service, and a room with wheelchair access according to the stay's information · what sets Baan Sook Aroon apart from the usual Khao Kho stay is that it is pet-friendly — per the information it accepts both dogs and cats, weighing up to about 10 kilograms each, with a pet fee of around 200 baht per night, which is not common in Khao Kho, so anyone who wants to bring their dog or cat along can stay with peace of mind · to be straight about it, there is no pool, gym or spa like a luxury resort (some sources list a few things, others do not specify, so ask the stay directly first if this matters to you) · the charm here is the view, the quiet, the cool air, and the friendly, owner-run holiday-home feel, more than a full set of amenities · anyone who wants a stay packed with on-site activities may need to plan to head out to the various spots around Khao Kho instead, which the location near the viewpoints makes easy to do

Food and breakfast — Baan Sook Aroon offers breakfast and has a shared kitchen where guests can cook for themselves, which is where a small stay like this is more flexible than a big hotel · per the information, breakfast comes in both American and Asian styles to choose from, possibly with an extra charge depending on the package you book, fitting for cool mornings up in the mountains, eaten with the view from the balcony or the garden · reviews on the food lean fairly positive in terms of warmth and freshness · what many people like is having a shared kitchen and BBQ corner, so you can buy ingredients and cook for yourself, with the feeling of staying at a holiday home with friends or family · that said, being a small stay, the menu options on site are not as varied as a big hotel, and other meals usually mean heading out · the tip from gathering reviews is that the Sadiao Phong and Khao Kho area is close to several restaurants and cafes with lovely views, both well-known Khao Kho coffee shops and local eateries, so a short drive out gives you plenty of options · if you are coming as a group and want dinner or a BBQ at the stay, arrange it or prepare the ingredients ahead, especially over long holidays when shops up the mountain may close early and run out of stock

Service — service is clearly the most praised part of Baan Sook Aroon in real reviews · many guests agree that the owner and staff are friendly, attentive in a personal way, and give the warm feeling of staying with relatives rather than a formal hotel · many were impressed that the team helps recommend spots around Khao Kho, helps with getting around, and looks after small details with genuine care · being a small stay makes the service feel thorough and personal, with no long queues like a big resort, and the service scores in real reviews stay consistently high · still, to be fair, being a small stay comes with limits — some services are not as precisely standardised as a hotel chain, and when it is full or short-staffed, the response on some things may be slower than expected · because it is a small, family-run stay, contacting them in advance through the page or by phone usually gets clearer, more flexible answers than booking through the system alone · but overall most voices put "friendly and warm service" among its top strengths, the thing that impresses people and makes them want to come back

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — pulling from Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com, Traveloka and several Khao Kho review pages, the picture is fairly consistent, with real review scores in the range of about 8.6 on Agoda/Trip.com up to around 9.3 on Booking.com (from a few hundred guests across several platforms), which is very good for a small, budget-friendly stay · on the praise side: every room has a private balcony where you see the sunrise and morning sea of fog right from the room, rooms are very clean, the owner and staff are friendly and warm, the atmosphere is quiet and good for resting, the air is cool and pleasant, the location is near the Khao Kho Palace viewpoint, the price is good value in the few-thousand-baht range, and it is a stay you can bring pets to · on the gripe side: the things that come up are that the stay is small and simple, with few rooms so it fills up fast in winter, the rooms are not sleek modern style, facilities are limited compared with a big resort (no pool, gym or spa), the location on the hillside has a steep and sometimes narrow climb, and soundproofing between rooms may not match a large building · most of these gripes are things you can manage by setting your expectations to match the price and type of stay rather than being big problems, and people who understand they are staying at a small budget place for the morning view are mostly happy with what they get, which is why review scores stay high

"A small stay but very clean, the room is lovely, open the balcony door in the morning and the sea of fog fills the whole valley — the best part of the trip · the owner is kind, you can bring your dog, and for a few thousand baht a view like this is more than worth it."

Price comparison and value — Baan Sook Aroon's starting price is around THB 1,000/night in regular periods, rising to about THB 1,800/night or more in the winter high season and on long holidays, depending on demand · compared with luxury resorts on the heights of Khao Kho that start in the several thousands up to five figures, Baan Sook Aroon is clearly in a different price bracket, and its value lies in getting the sunrise and sea-of-fog view from your own balcony for a few thousand baht, plus being pet-friendly with friendly service — a view that, at some resorts costing several thousand, you would still have to walk out to a viewpoint to see · for couples or small families whose main goal is to wake up to fog from the room and use Khao Kho as a base for visiting the various spots, a stay like this is far more worthwhile than paying more · but if you are coming to Khao Kho for luxury, modern-style rooms, a pool, or a full set of amenities, this may not be the answer, and you should look at the resorts on the higher ridges in a higher budget · put simply, Baan Sook Aroon suits people who weigh the morning view, the price, and bringing pets along over those buying luxury and a full set of amenities

What to know before booking — a few things will make the trip smoother · One, this is a small, budget-friendly stay with very few rooms, about 6, so set your expectations to match the type — come for the morning view, the quiet, the cool air and the friendly service, not for luxury · Two, if you plan to bring a pet, tell the stay and confirm the conditions directly first (weight up to about 10 kg, a fee of around 200 baht per night, numbers and house rules) to be sure · Three, because the rooms are few and popular for the view and the price, in winter (November–January) and on long holidays they fill up very fast, so book ahead and lock in free cancellation if your plans are not yet firm · Four, always pack warm clothes — the Sadiao Phong area of Khao Kho gets very cold in winter, genuinely cold at night and early morning, and check that the room you book has a water heater and thick blankets · Five, check your driving route up the mountain and that your vehicle is ready — the climb is steep and winding, narrow in places, and in the rainy season the fog rolls in thick with short visibility · Six, since it is a small, family-run stay, the most reliable way to book is through a major platform such as Agoda, Booking.com or Trip.com, or by calling the stay and its Facebook page (Baan.Sookaroon.Khaokho · tel. 087 849 4476) directly to confirm the price, room availability and the latest conditions

In summary — from all the real reviews, Baan Sook Aroon Khao Kho is the stay that suits best for couples, small families and pet lovers who want to wake up to a sea of fog from the room's balcony on a few-thousand-baht budget · its charm is that the name "Sook Aroon" matches what you actually get — the sunrise and sea of fog seen from your own balcony without going out to fight for a viewpoint, plus cleanliness, friendly holiday-home service, and being able to bring your dog or cat along, at a price that leaves plenty left over for sightseeing and eating · but if you are after a luxury resort with a pool, modern-style rooms, or a full set of amenities like a big hotel, this may not be the answer, and you should look at the hilltop resorts in a higher budget · for a budget Khao Kho trip whose heart is "the morning," though, Baan Sook Aroon meets that need squarely, which is why it keeps earning high review scores from guests who understand they are staying at a small, good-value place for a sea of fog you can see from the foot of the bed

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Baan Sook Aroon Khao Kho

faq.q: Where is Baan Sook Aroon Khao Kho · what is nearby?
faq.a: It sits on a hillside at 127 Moo 2, Sadiao Phong Subdistrict, Khao Kho District, Phetchabun Province · it is close to the Khao Kho Palace viewpoint at about 540 metres and View Ver Camp at about 980 metres · Khao Kho Palace, the Kanchanaphisek Pagoda and the wind-turbine field are all a short drive away · Wat Phra That Pha Sorn Kaew is further out towards Khaem Son, about 30 minutes' drive up · it is about 38 kilometres from Phetchabun town

faq.q: What is Baan Sook Aroon's starting price · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around THB 1,000/night in regular periods, rising to about THB 1,800/night or more in winter and on long holidays · it is a small stay of about 5–6 rooms, with Queen and King rooms with mountain-view balconies and a family room · rooms are few and fill up fast in high season, so compare several platforms and book ahead

faq.q: Can you really see the sea of fog from the room at Baan Sook Aroon · when is the best time to come?
faq.a: The main selling point is that every room has a private balcony facing the sunrise and the morning sea of fog, true to the name "Sook Aroon," so you can wake up to the view from the room without going out to fight for a viewpoint · the best time is late rainy season into early winter (November–January), when the air is cool and the chance of a sea of fog is high · rooms fill up very fast in this period, so book well ahead

faq.q: Can you bring pets to Baan Sook Aroon?
faq.a: Yes · this is a pet-friendly stay — per the information it accepts both dogs and cats, weighing up to about 10 kilograms each, with a pet fee of around 200 baht per night · because conditions can change, it is best to tell the stay and confirm directly before booking, including weight, numbers and house rules

faq.q: Who does Baan Sook Aroon suit best?
faq.a: It suits couples, small families and pet lovers who want a budget Khao Kho stay where you wake up to a sea of fog from the room's balcony, with a quiet atmosphere and friendly service · it is good for people who use Khao Kho as a base for getting out to the various spots · if you are hunting for a luxury resort with a pool or a full set of amenities, a hilltop resort may suit better

faq.q: What facilities and breakfast does Baan Sook Aroon have?
faq.a: It is a small stay that leans on simplicity · there is a shared kitchen, a BBQ corner, a garden lounge, a small convenience store, free Wi-Fi, free parking, a 24-hour front desk and laundry service · breakfast comes in both American and Asian styles (may carry an extra charge depending on the package) · there is no pool, gym or spa like a luxury resort, so if this matters, ask the stay first
